title: The gap between the two models
request:
b reads 0 a full ten ticks after a's write of 1 has been acknowledged

./your_program.sh consistency
init
op a write 1 0 10
op b read 0 20 30
check linearizable
check sequential
note: The same four operations, two different answers. Sequential consistency lets b's read be placed before a's write because they are different clients, and nothing in the model cares that the clock says otherwise. This is exactly what a stale read from a follower looks like, and exactly why 'strongly consistent' has to be said more precisely than that.

title: A history no ordering can rescue
request:
The same shape, but it is a reading its own earlier write

./your_program.sh consistency
init
op a write 1 0 10
op a read 0 20 30
check linearizable
check sequential
note: Program order is the one thing sequential consistency keeps, so a client that fails to see its own completed write cannot be explained by any reordering. That is the difference between a stale replica and a broken one.
